draft.title: The Battle of Actium
card: By 32 BC the Triumvirate had ended and Octavian and Mark Antony were rivals. Antony was allied with Cleopatra VII, the queen of Egypt. Octavian persuaded the Senate and people of Italy to declare war on Cleopatra.
In 31 BC the two fleets met at Actium, off the west coast of Greece. Octavian's fleet was led by his friend and general Agrippa.

Agrippa's ships cut off Antony's supplies, and Antony's forces were weakened by hunger and disease. Cleopatra and Antony broke through the blockade with part of their fleet and sailed for Egypt. Their remaining forces then surrendered.
Octavian followed them to Egypt in 30 BC. Antony and Cleopatra both died, and Egypt came under his control. With no rival left, Octavian was sole ruler of the Roman world.
draft.remember: Agrippa's naval victory at Actium removed Antony and Cleopatra, so Octavian had no rival left.

a.q: Why did Actium leave Octavian as sole ruler of Rome?
opts: His fleet defeated Antony, his last rival for power
The Senate named him the only heir to Caesar
Lepidus gave up his share of power to him
Cleopatra made peace and handed Egypt to him
a.why: Antony was the last rival with an army and a fleet. After Agrippa's victory and the fall of Egypt, nobody could challenge Octavian. The Senate naming him heir is wrong, because Caesar's will had named him heir years earlier.
a.clue: Think about who was left to oppose Octavian after the battle.

b.q: Which statement best explains how Octavian won at Actium?
opts: Agrippa blockaded Antony's fleet and cut off its supplies
Octavian led the fleet himself and destroyed it in battle
The Senate ordered Antony's soldiers to surrender
Cleopatra's fleet joined Octavian before the fighting began
b.why: Agrippa's blockade starved and weakened Antony's forces, and Antony and Cleopatra fled with part of their fleet. Octavian leading and destroying the fleet is the tempting wrong answer. The card says Agrippa led the fleet, and the victory came from the blockade, not a clash that destroyed it.
b.clue: Who led the fleet, and what did his ships do to Antony's supplies?

a.best: His fleet defeated Antony, his last rival for power

b.best: Agrippa blockaded Antony's fleet and cut off its supplies

problems.detail: The remember line says the victory at Actium 'removed Antony and Cleopatra'. The card says they broke through and escaped to Egypt, and only died in 30 BC after Octavian followed them. The line contradicts the card's sequence.
The clue ('Who led the fleet, and what did his ships do to Antony's supplies?') points straight to the Agrippa-blockade option, so students can answer without knowing the idea.

The why says the victory came 'from the blockade, not a clash'. Actium was a real naval battle on 2 September 31 BC, in which much of Antony's remaining fleet was burned or surrendered. The remember line itself calls it a 'naval victory'. Octavian was also present at the battle as overall commander, so 'not a clash' oversimplifies and could mislead.

proposal.title: The Battle of Actium
card: By 32 BC Octavian and Mark Antony were rivals. Antony was allied with Cleopatra VII, queen of Egypt, and Rome declared war on her.

Octavian held overall command, and his friend and general Agrippa led the fleet. At Actium, off the west coast of Greece, Agrippa's blockade cut Antony's supplies, and hunger and disease weakened his forces.
On 2 September 31 BC the fleets fought at sea. Antony and Cleopatra broke out with part of their fleet and fled to Egypt, and most of their remaining forces surrendered.
Octavian followed them to Egypt in 30 BC. Antony and Cleopatra both died, Egypt came under his control, and no rival with an army was left.
proposal.remember: Actium broke Antony's power at sea. His death in Egypt in 30 BC left Octavian with no rival.

a.q: Why did defeating Antony leave Octavian as sole ruler of Rome?
opts: Antony was his last rival with an army and a fleet
The Senate then named him the only heir to Caesar
Antony agreed to rule only the eastern provinces
Cleopatra made peace and handed Egypt to him
a.why: Antony was the last rival who could fight Octavian. Once he and Cleopatra died and Egypt fell in 30 BC, nobody was left to challenge him. The heir option is wrong, because Octavian had been Caesar's heir since 44 BC, and that did not remove his rivals.
a.clue: Think about who was left to oppose Octavian afterwards.

b.q: Which statement best describes how Octavian's side won at Actium?
opts: A blockade weakened Antony, then his fleet lost at sea
A single surprise attack on land destroyed Antony's army
The Senate's order made Antony's soldiers lay down arms
Cleopatra's ships changed sides as the fighting began
b.why: Agrippa's blockade left Antony's forces hungry and sick, and the sea battle on 2 September 31 BC finished the campaign. Cleopatra changing sides is the tempting wrong answer, but she broke out with Antony and fled to Egypt. The Senate did not end the war by order: it was won by fighting.
b.clue: The battle came at the end of a longer campaign.
